speaker: Doctor
text: I'll start by asking you a few questions to better understand your symptoms. Have you been experiencing any fever or chills along with the right flank pain and hematuria?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or shaking chills accompanying this pain, and does passing the urine feel painful or urgent? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC, CMP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance - Reddish, WBC - 10-20 /HPF, RBC - Too numerous to count, Nitrites - Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase - Positive; Urine Culture - Not in data; CBC - Within normal limits; CMP - Creatinine - 1.1 mg/dL, BUN - 14 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the WBCs, positive leukocyte esterase, and negative nitrites, do you have a history of kidney stones or does the pain radiate toward your groin? REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Renal Ultrasound: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the ultrasound findings of medullary cysts combined with your history of recurrent UTIs and visible blood in the urine, do you have a family history of kidney stones or renal failure? DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.
